latest_findings.claim: The exact rerun of the N=256, 3000-step config did not reproduce the original final margins. Seed 20: force 0.113 at layer 1 (R2 0.644 vs control 0.531), accel_step 0.162 (R2 0.926 vs control 0.765). Seed 21: force 0.003 (R2 0.586 vs control 0.583, below the bar), accel_step 0.198 (R2 0.912 vs control 0.714). Against the original {0.033, 0.040} force and {0.231, 0.245} accel_step margins, every accel_step margin is off by 0.033-0.083 and seed 20's force by more than 0.07. The schedule-horizon explanation is also refuted, because at step 3000 this 3000-step rerun matches the 6000-step runs (force 0.102 / 0.001) and the 12000-step runs (force 0.099 / 0.028, accel_step 0.162 / 0.202) to within about 0.025. The original 3000-step runs are the outlier, not the longer runs.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps. Their step-0 trajectories (accel_step trained R2 0.764 / 0.705, force 0.571 / 0.610) are identical to the 12000-step arm, so initialisation is reproducible. The hypothesis's expected-if-true outcome (match within 0.02) clearly failed, so the verdict is refuted. However, the expected-if-false reading ('nondeterminism of 0.03 or more') is not cleanly supported either. Under the current pipeline, runs with 3000, 6000 and 12000 total steps agree at step 3000 to within about 0.004 on accel_step and about 0.025 on force. That points to the original runs (f-20261013-000253-c709) being produced differently, not to large run-to-run noise. A likely cause is the accel_step control: it was 0.65-0.68 in the originals and is 0.71-0.76 here, while raw R2 is similar, which would account for most of the accel_step margin gap. This is inferred from summary numbers and has not been checked against the original runs' per-layer R2. The verdict would change if the original runs' raw trained R2 differed by more than 0.03 from these runs, or if a second identical rerun differed from this one by more than 0.03. Either result would make training nondeterminism the explanation. Seed 21's force sits at 0.001-0.003 from step 500 to 3000, even though val_mse_ratio is 0.899 at step 2000 and 0.282 at step 3000. So force onset does not cleanly follow val_mse_ratio < 1 in this run.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256 with 12000 training steps, force only just clears the bar in seed 20 and stays below it in seed 21. Seed 20 ends at force margin 0.105 at layer 1 (R2 0.636 vs control 0.531, required 0.100). Seed 21 ends at 0.087 at layer 2 (R2 0.673 vs control 0.585, required 0.100). From step 6000 to 12000 force gains +0.020 in seed 20 and +0.041 in seed 21, and seed 21's margin is still rising at 0.004 per 1000 steps at the end. accel_step stays stronger than force in both seeds: margin 0.181 at layer 3 (R2 0.946 vs control 0.765) and 0.218 at layer 4 (R2 0.932 vs control 0.714), with headroom-normalised margins of 0.769 and 0.762. val_mse_ratio is 0.062 and 0.045.
latest_findings.confidence_note:
Both runs finished all 12000 planned steps. Neither of the hypothesis's outcomes happened, so the result is inconclusive.

The 'true' outcome failed on three counts. Final force margins were 0.105 and 0.087, both below the 0.12 target. Seed 21 gained only 0.041 from step 6000 to 12000, against the 0.06 required. The onset test also failed. Seed 20's val_mse_ratio first fell below 1 at step 3500, went back above 1 at step 4000, and stayed below from step 4500. After that, its force margin never rose 0.03 above its value at that point (0.095 at step 3500, lowest 0.084 at step 5500). Seed 21's force margin was already climbing from step 1000 (0.001), before val_mse_ratio fell below 1 at step 3000 (0.822). Measured from step 3000, seed 21 only gained 0.03 at step 7500, 4500 steps later. The one prediction that held was accel_step's normalised margin, which landed inside [0.62, 0.77] in both seeds, though only just.

The 'false' outcome also failed. Seed 21 did end below 0.10, but its 6000-to-12000 gain of 0.041 is above the 0.03 limit, and neither seed has levelled off.

The training horizon is a strong confound. In the matched 6000-step run of exp-20261013-021753-c0b1, seed 20 had force margin 0.139 at step 6000. Here, at the same step, it is 0.085, and it ends lower (0.105) after twice the training. In that run seed 21 was flat at 0.001 through step 3000, while here it starts rising at step 1500. Either the lr schedule scales with total steps, or runs are not deterministic. Either way, cross-length comparisons of force are unreliable.

Seed 20 clears the bar by only 0.005, and seed 21's force control spread is 0.046, so whether force beats control at N=256 sits inside noise. What would change the verdict: seed 21 crossing 0.10, or both seeds clearly levelling off, in a run to about 18000 steps on a schedule-matched design. For comparison, N=128 reached 0.193-0.197 at 12000 steps (exp-20261013-031820-c873), so at that training length N=256 force is still about half of N=128's.

latest_findings.claim: With 12000 training steps at N=128, the best-layer force margin (layer 1, the distance layer) ends at 0.197 for seed 21 and 0.193 for seed 20. Both are just under the 0.20 N=64 band and above the 0.18 lower-ceiling cutoff. The gains from step 6000 to step 12000 were +0.029 and +0.019, and growth slowed over the run (6000-9000: +0.019/+0.011; 9000-12000: +0.010/+0.008). Over the same steps val_mse_ratio fell 7-11x (0.158->0.0137 and 0.102->0.0141). accel_step stays flat at layer 4 (raw margin 0.173->0.175 and 0.145->0.150; R2 0.932-0.933 against controls 0.757-0.783). Its headroom-normalised margin is 0.72 and 0.69, so force is still the weaker margin by headroom even though it is the only target that kept rising.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither pre-registered outcome happened in either seed. Supported needed a final margin >= 0.20 and a gain >= 0.03 in both seeds: both finals (0.19734 and 0.19309, unrounded) miss, and seed 20's gain of 0.019 misses. Refuted needed a final <= 0.18 and a gain <= 0.02: both finals miss. Seed 21's gain (~0.029, measured from a step-6000 value rounded to 0.168) is right at the 0.03 cutoff, but its final is below 0.20 either way. The horizon check passed: step-6000 force margins in these runs (0.168, 0.174) are within 0.005 of the 6000-step runs of the same seeds (0.163, 0.178), so the cross-run comparison is not horizon-confounded. The trajectories favour a slow approach to a ceiling near 0.20-0.21, below the N=64 seeds-20-21 values of 0.21-0.26 already reached by step 3000. That suggests a lower ceiling rather than just slower growth, but force was still gaining about 0.002-0.003 per 1000 steps at the end, so the asymptote is not pinned down. Other limits: two seeds, one data_seed, and best-of-3 controls. Force peaks at layer 1, the distance layer, where the distance margin is also creeping up (0.556->0.569 and 0.698->0.720), so this late gain may be a sharper distance read rather than an m2-weighted force code. Three results would change the verdict: a 24000-step run that clears 0.21 (slower growth), a run that levels off at <= 0.20 (lower ceiling), or N=64 seeds 20-21 trained to 12000 steps that rise well above 0.26 (confirms a gap between N=64 and N=128).

latest_findings.claim: At N=256 and 6000 steps, force did not stay flat, and it does not look like a ceiling either. Seed 20's force margin went from 0.102 at step 3000 to 0.139 at step 6000 (layer 1, R2 0.670 vs control 0.531; it first crossed the 0.1 bar at step 3000). Seed 21's went from 0.001 to 0.044 (R2 0.624 vs control 0.580), rising about +0.007 to +0.010 per 500 steps after it moved to layer 1 at step 3500. Both seeds were still rising at step 6000. accel_step behaved as predicted: its margin stayed flat (0.201 to 0.205 for seed 21, 0.158 to 0.163 for seed 20), giving headroom-normalized margins of 0.72 and 0.69, against 0.10 and 0.30 for force.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither the if-true nor the if-false outcome happened. The ceiling prediction needed a final force margin < 0.10 and a gain of <= 0.03 in both seeds. Seed 20 ended at 0.139, and both gains were above 0.03 (0.037 and 0.043). The if-false outcome needed a final margin >= 0.12 in both seeds or a gain of >= 0.06 in both. Seed 21 ended at 0.044, and neither gain reached 0.06. The accel_step half of the hypothesis held in both seeds, with normalized margins of 0.69 and 0.72, inside [0.62, 0.77]. The trajectories argue against a hard ceiling. Force was still climbing at step 6000 in both seeds, and the 3000-to-6000 gains here (0.037-0.043) are larger than at N=128 in the paired arm (0.022-0.031). That points to a later or slower start rather than a lower limit, but two seeds that disagree by about 0.1 can't settle it. Two things complicate the comparison with earlier work. First, the step-3000 force margins here (0.102 and 0.001) both differ from the 0.033-0.040 reported for the earlier 3000-step N=256 runs, so nondeterminism or an lr-schedule-horizon effect is still possible. Second, seed 21's force control_spread (0.054) is larger than seed 20's (0.025). Both runs completed all 6000 steps, and val_mse_ratio fell to 0.10-0.12, below 1 from step 3000 on. The verdict would become refuted if 12000-step runs took both seeds' force margin to >= 0.12. It would become supported if both levelled off below 0.10, or if a rerun showed that seed 20's step-3000 value of 0.102 is a nondeterministic outlier.

latest_findings.claim: At N=128 with training doubled to 6000 steps, the force margin was still rising slowly and did not reach the N=64 band (0.21-0.26). It ended at 0.178 for seed 20 (layer 1; R2 0.670 vs control 0.492) and 0.163 for seed 21 (best layer moving among 1, 2 and 4; R2 0.629 vs control 0.466). The gains from step 3000 to 6000 were +0.031 and +0.022, and neither curve has levelled off: the last 1000 steps added +0.009 and +0.007. accel_step was flat throughout, with margins 0.151 and 0.170 and headroom-normalised margins of about 0.70 in both seeds (R2 0.934 vs control 0.783; 0.927 vs 0.757). That fits the expected [0.62, 0.77] range. Normalised force margins were only 0.35 and 0.31, so on both raw and normalised margin accel_step leads force.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither pre-registered outcome happened. The supported case needed a final margin >= 0.20 and a gain >= 0.04 in both seeds; both seeds fall short on both. The refuted case needed a final margin <= 0.17 and a gain <= 0.02 in both seeds. Seed 20 ends at 0.178 with a +0.031 gain, and seed 21's gain of +0.022 is just over the 0.02 limit. The result is a third pattern the hypothesis did not set out: steady growth of about 0.004-0.005 per 500 steps, with no plateau and no catch-up. Over the same span val_mse_ratio fell 5-9x (0.24/0.14 at step 3000 to 0.027/0.030 at step 6000). The step-3000 checkpoints match the earlier 3000-step runs to within 0.003 (seed 20: 0.147 vs 0.150) and 0.010 (seed 21: 0.141 vs 0.131). That is under the 0.03 rule, so cross-run comparison is valid and the lr-schedule horizon has little visible effect at N=128. Both runs completed 6000/6000 steps, and checkpoints were every 500 steps. If growth stays linear, seed 20 would reach 0.20 at roughly 8000-9000 steps and seed 21 at roughly 10000-11000. A 12000-step run would separate 'slower growth' from 'lower ceiling'. The verdict would change to supported if force reached >= 0.20 in both seeds by then, and to refuted if both levelled off below 0.18. With only two seeds, and seed 21's best force layer changing between checkpoints (likely a flat per-layer profile), the per-seed numbers are noisy at the 0.01-0.02 level.

config.expected_if_false: In at least one seed the final force margin is >= 0.21, within 0.03 of the N=64 value for that seed, so the N=128 drop seen in seeds 20-21 is seed-specific. Or in at least one seed it is <= 0.06, close to N=256, which would mean the decline is steeper than gradual-in-log-N.
config.expected_if_true: In both seeds the final force margin is in [0.08, 0.20] and at least 0.04 below the same seed's N=64 value (0.247 for seed 22, 0.234 for seed 23). accel_step's headroom-normalised margin is in [0.62, 0.77].
config.hypothesis: The intermediate N=128 force margin at 3000 steps (0.150 for seed 20, 0.131 for seed 21) replicates on fresh seeds. Seeds 22-23 at N=128, with architecture, data and 3000-step training matched to the N=64 seeds 22-23 arm (exp-20261013-011737-dff2: force 0.247 / 0.234), give a final best-layer force margin well below their N=64 values and well above N=256 (0.033-0.040). The headroom-normalised accel_step margin is the same as at N=64 (0.68-0.70). Margins are read from the per-checkpoint trajectory using unrounded values against a strict >= required_margin bar, with force taken at its best layer at each checkpoint.
